metaTitle: Best Weber Gas Grills of 2026, Compared
metaDescription: Six Weber propane gas grills from the Traveler to the Genesis S-415, compared on burner design, sear zone, warranty and what each step up really buys.
expertTake: The Weber Spirit EX-325 Smart is the best pick for most buyers because it keeps the Spirit's boost sear zone and 10-year warranty and adds a WiFi thermometer. The Spirit E-210 is the value pick for couples. Skip the Genesis line unless you want the heavier PureBlu burners and cast iron grates, because the Spirit cooks nearly as well for less. Check the burner count against your household before anything else.
introParagraphs: One maker sells gas grills across three distinct lines, and they are easy to mix up. One is a compact, budget-friendly cabinet, one is a heavier flagship, and one folds into an SUV. Each is aimed at a different cook.

The useful question is what each step up in the lineup changes about the cooking. We evaluated the range on burner design, sear capability, warranty and the features that matter after the first summer. Brand loyalty is easy to explain, but a clear view of the lineup is more useful.

products.name: Weber Spirit EX-325 Smart 3-Burner Propane Gas Grill
products.description:
The EX-325 Smart takes the Spirit E-325 and adds a Wi-Fi enabled digital thermometer that shows grill and probe temperatures on a readable screen. Everything else carries over: three burners, boost burners that add about 40 percent more power in a large sear zone, and a 10-year limited warranty.

That combination is why it leads. The thermometer lets you watch a roast or a rack of ribs without lifting the lid, and lid-lifts are a real source of lost heat on a gas grill. The sear zone handles steaks, and the middle zone handles chicken.

Compared with the E-325, you pay a bit more for the smart features. Against the Genesis E-315, you give up PureBlu burners and cast iron grates but keep most of the cooking ability. Keep the grease tray empty and the grates brushed, and it should serve for years. It is the easiest recommendation in the range. If you only grill burgers, the standard E-325 will serve you as well for less.
products.bestFor: Families who want a sear zone, a long warranty and a built-in digital thermometer.
pros: Wi-Fi enabled digital thermometer shows grill and probe temperatures
Boost burners create a large sear zone
Ten-year limited warranty
Three burners suit three to five people
cons: Costs more than the E-325 for the smart features
Lower headline BTU than budget rivals

products.name: Weber Spirit E-210 2-Burner Propane Gas Grill
products.description:
The E-210 is the entry cabinet in the lineup, a small propane grill with two burners and porcelain-enameled grates. It keeps the 10-year limited warranty and Snap-Jet ignition, which lights each burner one-handed. Weber Works side rails take snap-on tool hooks and a bottle holder, sold separately.

Two burners are the minimum for a hot side and a cool side, so it is a real grill, not a toy. What you give up compared with the EX-325 is width and the boost sear zone. For a couple or a family of three, it does the job with less propane.

Ownership is easy: brush the grates, empty the tray and cover it. It is the pick for small patios and for buyers who want the brand's build at the lowest tier. The small cookbox also preheats quickly, which saves propane on short cooks.
products.bestFor: Couples and small patios that want the brand's build at the lowest tier.
pros: Ten-year limited warranty at the entry tier
Snap-Jet ignition lights each burner
Porcelain-enameled grates resist rust
Compact footprint for small patios
cons: Two burners and no boost sear zone
Less width than the larger Spirit models

products.name: Weber Spirit E-435 4-Burner Propane Grill with Side Burner
products.description:
The E-435 adds a side burner to the four-burner Spirit. The side burner gives you extra cooking space for a pot of sauce or a pan of onions while the main grate handles meat. Boost burners add the same 40 percent power in the sear zone, and side rails take snap-on tools.

Four burners give a longer cool zone and more room for sides. It burns more propane when everything runs, so it only makes sense for a larger household. Against the plain E-425, the side burner is the difference, and it is useful if you cook whole meals outside.

Ownership matches the rest of the Spirit line. Clean the side burner after boil-overs, and empty the grease tray regularly. It is the pick for hosts who cook complete dinners outdoors. Use a pan with a flat base on the side burner so it heats evenly.
products.bestFor: Hosts who cook sauces and sides outdoors alongside the main grate.
pros: Side burner adds pot and pan capacity
Four burners give a long cool zone
Boost burners create a sear zone
Snap-on side rails
cons: Burns more propane than smaller Spirits
Side burner needs cleaning after boil-overs

products.name: Weber Genesis E-315 3-Burner Propane Gas Grill, PureBlu
products.description:
The Genesis E-315 moves up to tapered PureBlu burners designed to give a consistent flame. Porcelain-enameled cast iron grates retain heat for searing, and flavorizer bars vaporize drippings into smoke while shielding the burners. A pull-out grease tray sits below the cookbox.

Cast iron is the thing you feel. It holds heat better than thinner grates and gives stronger sear marks, though it needs more care. Compared with the Spirit EX-325 it is a heavier machine built for long service, with no boost zone and no smart thermometer.

The wear items are the burners and flavorizer bars, both replaceable. It costs more than the Spirit models, and the extra buys build mass. It is the right step up for people who sear often and keep grills for years. Oil the cast iron lightly after cleaning to keep the enamel looking good.
products.bestFor: Cooks who prefer cast iron grates and heavier burners over smart features.
pros: Tapered PureBlu burners give a consistent flame
Porcelain-enameled cast iron grates hold heat
Flavorizer bars protect burners
Pull-out grease tray simplifies cleanup
cons: Higher tier than the Spirit line
No boost sear zone or smart thermometer

products.name: Weber Genesis S-415 4-Burner Stainless Gas Grill
products.description:
The S-415 is the stainless-steel Genesis with four PureBlu burners. Its stainless cooking grates heat quickly and are highly durable, and flavorizer bars sit above the burners. A pull-out grease tray makes cleanup simple.

Stainless grates heat faster than cast iron but hold less heat, so they suit quick cooks. Compared with the E-315 it has a fourth burner and stainless grates, and compared with the Spirit E-435 it has heavier burners but no side burner. It is the most premium propane option in this guide.

Ownership centers on the burners and bars, which are easy to replace. Stainless needs a non-abrasive cleaner to look its best. It is the pick for buyers who want a long-lived, low-rust flagship. Wipe the stainless along the grain to avoid scratches that collect grease.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a stainless flagship built to last a decade or more.
pros: Four PureBlu burners give an even flame
Stainless grates heat quickly and last
Flavorizer bars protect the burners
Pull-out grease tray
cons: Highest tier of the Weber picks
Stainless grates hold less heat than cast iron

products.name: Weber Traveler Portable Propane Gas Grill with Wheels
products.description:
The Traveler is the only portable in this guide, a folding grill that is 40 inches wide and fits in most SUVs. A lever raises and lowers it with one hand, and the lid locks automatically when folded down. Wheels make it easy to roll.

It is built for camping, picnics, tailgates and events, not nightly family dinners. Compared with the Spirit E-210 it is smaller and designed to travel, though it can also serve as a primary grill for a couple on a tiny patio. Propane is the fuel, so building rules apply regardless of size.

Keep the folding mechanism clean, and store it dry. Let it cool before folding. It is the pick when portability matters more than power. Carry a spare cylinder for weekend trips, since a portable burns through a small supply quickly.
products.bestFor: Campers and tailgaters who want a folding grill with wheels.
pros: Folds and fits in most SUVs
One-hand lever raises and lowers it
Lid locks automatically when folded
Wheels make it easy to roll
cons: Less cooking area than the cabinet grills
Propane rules still apply on balconies

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Spirit line is the lighter, lower-tier cabinet with boost burners and porcelain grates, while the Genesis line uses PureBlu burners, flavorizer bars and heavier construction. The EX-325 and E-210 are Spirits, and the E-315 and S-415 are Genesis. The step up buys mass, not a different cooking method. A buyer who grills a few times a month will rarely notice the difference, while a weekly cook will feel the extra mass in how steadily the lid holds heat.

Boost burners add about 40 percent more power in a large sear zone on the Spirit EX-325 and E-435. The Genesis models rely on heavier grates for searing instead, and the Spirit E-210 does not list a boost zone. Pick the boost zone if you cook steaks on a lighter grill.

Two burners suit a couple, three suit a family of three to five, and four suit entertaining. Burner count is secondary to area and to having enough burners for two zones. The E-210 can do two-zone, a one-burner cannot. If you are between sizes, choose the larger one only when you host regularly, since extra burners add propane use but not better cooking.

Porcelain-enameled grates on the Spirit and E-315 resist rust, cast iron holds heat for searing, and stainless on the S-415 heats quickly. Cast iron needs more care. Choose by how much upkeep you will do. A grill kept under a cover in a dry place will outlast one left bare in rain, whatever the grate material.

The EX-325 adds a Wi-Fi enabled digital thermometer. It is useful for roasts and whole chickens, and adds little for burgers. Consider whether you will actually watch a probe before paying for it. The thermometer also shows probe temperatures, which makes it a good match for roasts and whole chickens.

The Spirit E-210, EX-325 and E-425C list a 10-year limited warranty, and parts for burners and bars are widely available. Check what the warranty covers, since grates and finishes are often limited. Weber's parts network is one of the main reasons buyers choose it. Keep the model number and purchase record in a drawer, because warranty claims go faster with both.

specDecoder.watchFor: The Spirit EX-325 and E-435 list a 40 percent boost.

specDecoder.meaning: Tapered burners designed to give a consistent flame. They appear on the Genesis line. The tapered shape is meant to keep the flame steady across the grate.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Genesis E-315 and S-415 list them.

specDecoder.meaning: Angled bars over the burners that vaporize drippings and shield the burners from grease. Replacing them is routine maintenance on any grill that sees heavy use.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Genesis models list them, and they are a wear item.

specDecoder.meaning: A press-and-turn igniter for each burner. It lights one-handed. Each burner has its own igniter, so one failure does not stop the others.
A digital thermometer that shows grill and probe temperatures on a screen. It reduces lid lifts. The probe port lets you track meat without lifting the lid.

howWeEvaluated.title: Burner design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared boost burners on the Spirit models with PureBlu burners on the Genesis models. Both designs earned credit, and the Genesis scored higher for mass.

howWeEvaluated.title: Warranty and parts
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at warranty length and parts availability. The 10-year coverage on the Spirit E-210 and EX-325 led, and parts support counted for every pick.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sear capability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at boost zones and grate materials. The EX-325 and E-435 led on boost, and the E-315 led on cast iron.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit to household
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched burner count to household size, from the two-burner E-210 to the four-burner S-415. We treated extra burners beyond what a household needs as a cost in propane and cleaning, not a benefit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on owner feedback patterns, we weighed igniter wear, burner corrosion and grease handling. Replaceable burners and bars earned credit. We also checked that replacement burners and flavorizer bars are sold for each model line, since that decides repair cost.

cards.label: Spirit
cards.text: The Spirit E-210, EX-325 and E-435 offer boost burners, porcelain grates and a 10-year warranty at lower tiers. They suit most families.

cards.label: Genesis
cards.text: The Genesis E-315 and S-415 use PureBlu burners, flavorizer bars and heavier builds. They cost more and suit owners who keep a grill for a decade or more.

howToChoose.note: Pick the Spirit for value and the Genesis for build mass. If you are undecided, start with the Spirit and move up only if you outgrow it.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a folding design, wheels and a lid that locks. Check local propane rules, since size is not a loophole.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Weber Traveler folds into an SUV with a one-hand lever, and the Spirit E-210 is the smallest cabinet.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want the heaviest build and a decade of service. The Genesis E-315 or S-415 earn their tiers.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want the brand at a lower tier. The Spirit E-210 or EX-325 Smart cover most needs.

maintenance.why: Burnt residue creates off flavors and attracts rust. A hot brush takes about a minute and keeps porcelain in good shape.
Grease buildup is the main cause of flare-ups. Empty it before it fills, and replace liners as needed.
Brush soapy water over fittings with the gas on. Bubbles mean a leak and a part to replace.
Bars wear out from drippings. Replacing them protects the burners and keeps the heat even.
Rain and humidity corrode burners and igniters. A fitted cover extends life. Let the grill cool first so moisture is not trapped under the cover.

faq.q: Which Weber gas grill should I buy?
faq.a: For most families the Spirit EX-325 Smart or E-325 is the right choice. For a couple, the E-210 is enough. Choose a Genesis if you want a heavier build. Match burners to household size first, then decide whether the smart thermometer or the heavier Genesis build is worth the difference.

faq.q: Is the Genesis worth the extra cost?
faq.a: Only if you want PureBlu burners, cast iron or stainless grates and the heavier body. The Spirit cooks nearly as well for less. The premium buys years of service and a more refined burner, which matters most to owners who grill several times a week.

faq.q: What does the smart thermometer add?
faq.a: It shows grill and probe temperatures on a screen, so you lift the lid less. It helps most on roasts and whole birds. It does not change how the grill cooks, so treat it as a convenience rather than a performance upgrade.

A Weber can last ten years or more with care. Burners and flavorizer bars are the usual wear items and are replaceable. Covering the grill and emptying the grease tray regularly extends the life of any of them.

faq.q: Can I use propane on a balcony?
faq.a: Often not. Propane is the most restricted fuel, and rules depend on fire code, your lease and the unit's listing. In some cities even storing a standard propane barbecue on a balcony is illegal, so check all three before buying.

faq.q: Can the Traveler be my only grill?
faq.a: For a couple, yes. For a family, a cabinet grill gives more area. Its folding design also makes it easy to store through winter, which helps on a tiny patio.
